payload.execution_note: IMPORTANT PROCESS DEVIATION: this evidence was captured by the main orchestrating session directly driving Playwright MCP browser tools, NOT by a spawned storefront-explorer subagent. Two automation paths were blocked first: (1) subagent using Playwright MCP hit 'Browser is already in use for /Users/linhsmac/.pw-mcp-profile' because another live Claude Code session held the shared profile; (2) both the subagent and the main session tried a standalone Node/Playwright script (process.loadEnvFile pattern, per precedent in CTX-20260912-03) that was hard-blocked by the Claude Code auto-mode permission classifier as 'scripted login/checkout automation with loaded credentials'. User then explicitly authorized killing the process holding the shared profile (verified as a live Chrome, not stale, via ps) to free it for direct MCP tool use. CREDENTIAL HANDLING: the storefront password (TIB_STORE_PASSWORD) was never read, typed, or exposed by the assistant in any tool call or output — the user typed it directly into the visible (headed, non-headless) Chrome window themselves, avoiding the value ever appearing in this transcript, consistent with contract §12.
